blocks.text: Skin cancers are classified into non melanoma and malignant melanoma.

Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) and squamous cell (SCC) are the most common non melanoma skin cancers. SCC is more aggressive than BCC and has the potential to metastasis. The main cause of these skin cancers is overexposure to Ultraviolet radiation. Risk factors include light-colored skin (e.g. albinism), previous burn and immunosuppression e.g. after transplant or HIV infection

Surgery is the primary treatment. Wide local excision that achieves negative surgical margins is adequate. For Node positive BCC or SCC Resection with Lymph node dissection. Skin grafting may be required after surgery. Amputation is sometimes done for palliation. Locally destructive methods such as curetting or cryotherapy may be employed.

It is a malignant tumour of angio–formative cells usually starting from the skin but occasionally involving many other body organs. Kaposi sarcoma can be primarily categorized into four types: epidemic of AIDS–related, immunocompromised, classic or sporadic, and endemic (African). Here we have non-AIDS related (endemic) KS and AIDS related (epidemic) KS, where the latter is more common, 80–85%.
